ACTAttractor.citation: Arneodo, A., Coullet, P., Tresser, C. (1981). A possible new mechanism for the onset of turbulence. Physics Letters A 81, 197-201.
ACTAttractor.description: A symmetric Lorenz-like normal form for the onset of turbulence through a cascade of homoclinic bifurcations, with cubic and quadratic terms absent from the Lorenz equations.

AFMCantilever.citation: Ashhab, M., Salapaka, M. V., Dahleh, M., Mezic, I. (1999). Melnikov-based dynamical analysis of microcantilevers in scanning probe microscopy. Nonlinear Dynamics 20, 197-220.
AFMCantilever.description: Single-mode model of a sinusoidally driven atomic force microscope cantilever interacting with the sample through a Lennard-Jones force (van der Waals attraction and short-range repulsion). The forcing amplitude lies in the chaotic range given by Davaie-Markazi and Sohanian-Haghighi (2011).

AnishchenkoAstakhov.citation: Anishchenko, et al. Nonlinear dynamics of chaotic and stochastic systems: tutorial and modern developments. 2007.

ArecchiFeedbackLaser.citation: Meucci, R., Euzzor, S., Arecchi, F. T., Ginoux, J.-M. (2021). Minimal universal model for chaos in laser with feedback. International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos 31, 2130013. Based on Arecchi, F. T., Gadomski, W., Meucci, R. (1986). Physical Review A 34, 1617-1620.
ArecchiFeedbackLaser.description: A CO2 laser with electro-optic feedback from the output intensity to the cavity losses: laser intensity, population inversion and feedback voltage. The canonical laboratory example of Shilnikov homoclinic chaos. Stiff; the chaotic window in b0 is narrow.

Arneodo.citation: Arneodo, A., Coullet, P. & Tresser, C. Occurence of strange attractors in three-dimensional Volterra equations. Physics Letters A 79, 259--263 (1980)
Arneodo.description: A modified Lotka-Volterra ecosystem, also known as the ACT attractor.

ArneodoVolterra.citation: Arneodo, A., Coullet, P., Tresser, C. (1980). Occurrence of strange attractors in three-dimensional Volterra equations. Physics Letters A 79, 259-263. Equivalent to four-strategy replicator dynamics: Skyrms, B. (1992). Journal of Logic, Language and Information 1, 111-130.
ArneodoVolterra.description: A three-species Lotka-Volterra community with mixed competition and predation, the canonical chaotic Lotka-Volterra system and, by Hofbauer's transformation, the minimal chaotic replicator dynamics of evolutionary game theory.

ArnoldBeltramiChildress.citation: V. I. Arnold, Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics 30, 223 (1966).
ArnoldBeltramiChildress.description: An exact solution of Euler's equation for inviscid flow in 3D. Often referred to as the ABC flow.

ArnoldWeb.citation: Froeschle, C., Guzzo, M. & Legga, E (2000). Graphical evolution of the Arnold web: From order to chaos. Science 289.
ArnoldWeb.description: A quasi-integrable system that transitions to Chirikov diffusive dynamics when perturbed.

AtmosphericRegime.citation: Tuwankotta (2006). Chaos in a coupled oscillators system with widely spaced frequencies and energy-preserving non-linearity
AtmosphericRegime.description: A model of regime transition in atmospheric flows. Contains widely-separated timescales due a quadratic term, which itself arises from a conservation law.

AzizAlaouiLeslieGower.citation: Aziz-Alaoui, M. A. (2002). Study of a Leslie-Gower-type tritrophic population model. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals 14, 1275-1293. Parameters from Bandyopadhyay, M. et al. (2008). Nonlinear Analysis: Modelling and Control 13, 305-324.
AzizAlaouiLeslieGower.description: A tritrophic chain of logistic prey, a specialist predator with a Holling type II response, and a sexually reproducing generalist top predator with Leslie-Gower losses. All three densities are stored as logarithms because the specialist predator falls to about 1e-8.

BateHilker.citation: Bate, A. M., Hilker, F. M. (2013). Complex dynamics in an eco-epidemiological model. Bulletin of Mathematical Biology 75, 2059-2078.
BateHilker.description: A Rosenzweig-MacArthur predator-prey system with a frequency-dependent infectious disease in the predator: prey density, predator density and the infected fraction of predators. All three are stored as logarithms, as in the paper, because the predator falls to about 1e-9. Parameters follow the paper's Fig. 8 with disease-induced mortality mu = 14.

BeerRNN.citation: Beer, R. D. (1995). On the dynamics of small continuous-time recurrent neural networks. Adapt. Behav., 3(4), 4692013509.
BeerRNN.description: A two-neuron minimal model nervous system.

BelousovZhabotinsky.citation: Gyorgyi and Field (1992). A three-variable model of deterministic chaos in the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction. Nature.
BelousovZhabotinsky.description: A reduced-order model of the BZ reaction that exhibits period doubling. The bifurcation parameter for controlling the onset of chaos is kf. The system undergoes regular cycling when kf=3e-4, and chaotic oscillations when kf=3.5e-4

BetaCellBurster.citation: Mosekilde, E., Lading, B., Yanchuk, S., Maistrenko, Y. (2001). Bifurcation structure of a model of bursting pancreatic cells. BioSystems 63, 3-13. Based on Sherman, A., Rinzel, J., Keizer, J. (1988). Biophysical Journal 54, 411-425.
BetaCellBurster.description: Electrical bursting of an insulin-secreting pancreatic beta-cell, with an instantaneously activated calcium current, a delayed-rectifier potassium current and a slow voltage-gated potassium current. Time is in seconds and voltage in mV. Stiff, with a slow-to-fast time-scale ratio of about 6e-4.

BickleyJet.citation: Hadjighasem, Karrasch, Teramoto, Haller (2016). A Spectral Clustering Approach to Lagrangian Vortex Detection Phys Rev E.
BickleyJet.description: A zonal jet passing between two rows of counter-rotating vortices: a steady Hamiltonian with three travelling-wave perturbations. Lengths in Mm and time in days; the zonal coordinate is periodic with period 2 pi / k1 (20 Mm). The stored initial condition is in the chaotic sea of the northern vortex row.

Blasius.description: A chaotic food web composed of interacting predators,, consumers, and vegetation.

BlasiusHuppertStone.citation: Blasius, B., Huppert, A., Stone, L. (1999). Complex dynamics and phase synchronization in spatially extended ecological systems. Nature 399, 354-359. See also Blasius, B., Stone, L. (2000). International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos 10, 2361-2380.
BlasiusHuppertStone.description: A vegetation-herbivore-predator food chain whose oscillations keep a nearly constant phase while their peak heights vary chaotically (uniform phase, chaotic amplitude), the standard model of phase synchronization in ecological populations.

BlinkingRotlet.citation: Meleshko & Aref. A blinking rotlet model for chaotic advection. Physics of Fluids 1996. See also Tallapragada and Sudarsanam PRE 2019
BlinkingRotlet.description: The location of the mixer is chosen so that there is a stagnation point at its symmetric complement. Solution is given in polar coordinates (r, theta).

BlinkingVortex.citation: Aref (1984). Stirring by chaotic advection. J. Fluid Mechanics.
BlinkingVortex.description: A classic minimal chaotic mixing flow. Solution is given in polar coordinates (r, theta)

Bouali.citation: Bouali (1999). Feedback loop in extended Van der Pols equation applied to an economic model of cycles. International Journal of Bifurkation and Chaos, Vol. 9, No. 4
Bouali.description: Economic cycles with fluctuating demand. Related to the DequanLi attractor

Bouali2.citation: Bouali (1999). Feedback loop in extended Van der Pols equation applied to an economic model of cycles. International Journal of Bifurkation and Chaos, Vol. 9, No. 4

BurkeShaw.description: A scroll-like attractor with unique symmetry along the z axis.

CaTwoPlus.citation: Houart, Dupont, Goldbeter. Bull Math Biol 1999.

CaTwoPlusQuasiperiodic.citation: Houart, Dupont, Goldbeter. Bull Math Biol 1999.
CaTwoPlusQuasiperiodic.description: Intracellular calcium ion oscillations with quasiperiodic parameter values. The original paper also includes parameters for a limit cycle

CarrollRossler.citation: Carroll, T. L. (1995). A simple circuit for demonstrating regular and synchronized chaos. American Journal of Physics 63, 377-379.
CarrollRossler.description: A piecewise-linear electronic circuit that behaves like the Rossler system, widely used in chaos-synchronization experiments. Time is scaled by the circuit rate (10^4 per second).

CellCycle.description: A simplified model of the cell cycle. The parameter `Kim` controls the bifurcations.

CellularNeuralNetwork.citation: Arena, Caponetto, Fortuna, and Porto., Int J Bifurcat Chaos. 1998:  1527-1539.

Chen.citation: Chen (1997). Proc. First Int. Conf. Control of Oscillations and Chaos.
Chen.description: A system based on feedback anti-control in engineering.

ChenLee.citation: Chen HK, Lee CI (2004). Anti-control of chaos in rigid body motion. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals
ChenLee.description: A rigid body with feedback anti-control.

Chua.citation: Chua, L. O. (1969) Introduction to Nonlinear Network Theory, McGraw-Hill, New York.
Chua.description: An electronic circuit with a diode providing negative resistance.

ChuaCubic.citation: Huang, A., Pivka, L., Wu, C. W., Franz, M. (1996). Chua's equation with cubic nonlinearity. International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos 6, 2175-2222. See also Zhong, G.-Q. (1994). IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I 41, 934-941.
ChuaCubic.description: Chua's circuit with a smooth cubic nonlinear resistor in place of the piecewise-linear one, producing a double-scroll attractor.

CircadianRhythm.citation: Leloup, Gonze, Goldbeter. 1999. Gonze, Leloup, Goldbeter. 2000
CircadianRhythm.description: The Drosophila circadian rhythm under periodic light/dark forcing.

CoevolvingPredatorPrey.description: A system of predator-prey equations with co-evolving prey.

Colpitts.citation: Kennedy (2007). IEEE Trans Circuits & Systems. 1994: 771-774. Li, Zhou, Yang. Chaos, Solitons, & Fractals.
Colpitts.description: An electrical circuit used as a signal generator.

ConsecutiveAutocatalator.citation: Lynch, D. T. (1992). Chaotic behavior of reaction systems: mixed cubic and quadratic autocatalysis. Chemical Engineering Science 47, 4435-4444.
ConsecutiveAutocatalator.description: An isothermal continuous stirred tank reactor with consecutive quadratic and cubic autocatalytic steps (A + B to D + 2B, D + 2B to 3B) and decay of the autocatalyst. The attractor is screw-type with a non-unimodal return map.

ConsecutiveReactionCSTR.citation: Kahlert, C., Rossler, O. E., Varma, A. (1981). Chaos in a continuous stirred tank reactor with two consecutive first-order reactions, one exo-, one endothermic. Springer Series in Chemical Physics 18, 355-365. See also Chemburkar, R. M., Rossler, O. E., Varma, A. (1987). Chemical Engineering Science 42, 1507-1509.
ConsecutiveReactionCSTR.description: A nonisothermal continuous stirred tank reactor running the consecutive reactions A to B (exothermic) and B to C (endothermic), with Arrhenius kinetics and jacket cooling. Dimensionless concentrations of A and B and reactor temperature.

Coullet.citation: Arneodo, A., Coullet, P. & Tresser, C. Occurence of strange attractors in three-dimensional volterra equations. Physics Letters A 79, 259--263 (1980)
Coullet.description: A variant of the Arneodo attractor

Dadras.citation: S Dadras, HR Momeni (2009). A novel three-dimensional autonomous chaotic system generating two, three and four-scroll attractors. Physics Letters A.
Dadras.description: An electronic circuit capable of producing multiple attractors under bifurcations.

DarukaDitlevsen.citation: Daruka, I., Ditlevsen, P. D. (2016). A conceptual model for glacial cycles and the middle Pleistocene transition. Climate Dynamics 46, 29-40.
DarukaDitlevsen.description: A conceptual glacial-cycle model: a climate state variable in a skewed quartic potential with integrated memory, forced by obliquity insolation that couples multiplicatively through the ice-albedo effect. Time is scaled so that the forcing period is 10.

DengLoladze.citation: Deng, B., Loladze, I. (2007). Competitive coexistence in stoichiometric chaos. Chaos 17, 033108.
DengLoladze.description: A producer grazed by two consumers in which phosphorus limits both the producer's carrying capacity and the consumers' food quality through Liebig minimum terms. Chaos allows the two consumers to coexist on a single resource. Carbon in mg/L, time in days.

DequanLi.description: Related to the Three Scroll unified attractor TSUCS-2

DoubleGyre.citation: Shadden, Lekien, Marsden (2005). Definition and properties of Lagrangian coherent structures from finite-time Lyapunov exponents in two-dimensional aperiodic flows. Physica D.
DoubleGyre.description: A time-dependent fluid flow exhibiting Lagrangian coherent structures

DoublePendulum.citation: See, for example: Marion (2013). Classical dynamics of particles and systems.
DoublePendulum.description: Two point masses on massless rigid rods, without damping. The state is the two angles from the downward vertical and their canonical momenta; the outer pendulum rotates over the top.

DoubleScrollJerk.citation: Elwakil, A. S., Kennedy, M. P. (2001). Construction of classes of circuit-independent chaotic oscillators using passive-only nonlinear devices. IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I 48, 289-307.
DoubleScrollJerk.description: A jerk equation with a signum nonlinearity, realisable with passive nonlinear devices, producing a double-scroll attractor.

DrivenAlfven.citation: Hada, T., Kennel, C. F., Buti, B., Mjolhus, E. (1990). Chaos in driven Alfven systems. Physics of Fluids B 2, 2581-2590. See also Chian, A. C.-L. et al. (2007). Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics 14, 17-29.
DrivenAlfven.description: Stationary nonlinear Alfven waves of the derivative nonlinear Schrodinger equation with resistive damping and a circularly polarized driver, a model of intermittent Alfvenic turbulence in the solar wind.

DrivenPendulum.citation: Baker, G. L., Gollub, J. P. (1996). Chaotic Dynamics: An Introduction, 2nd ed. Cambridge University Press. See also Gwinn, E. G., Westervelt, R. M. (1985). Intermittent chaos and low-frequency noise in the driven damped pendulum. Physical Review Letters 54, 1613.
DrivenPendulum.description: A sinusoidally driven, damped rigid pendulum with the full sine nonlinearity; the canonical textbook chaotic oscillator. The angle variable is unbounded (rotations) and is mapped through a sine.

Duffing.citation: Duffing, G. (1918), Forced oscillations with variable natural frequency and their technical relevance, Heft 41/42, Braunschweig: Vieweg.
Duffing.description: A monochromatically-forced rigid pendulum, with the nonlinearity approximated as cubic.

DynamicHallInstability.citation: Hupper, G., Scholl, E. (1991). Dynamic Hall effect as a mechanism for self-sustained oscillations and chaos in semiconductors. Physical Review Letters 66, 2372-2375.
DynamicHallInstability.description: Impact-ionization breakdown in p-type germanium in crossed electric and magnetic fields: dielectric relaxation of the longitudinal and Hall fields coupled to the free-carrier density. Fields in V/cm, density in units of 1e7 per cubic centimetre, time in microseconds; nstar is the steady carrier density at the control field exs. The control field exs = 3.12 V/cm lies in the first chaotic band of the reproduced bifurcation sequence, which is shifted by about 0.07 V/cm from the paper's.

DynasticCycle.citation: Feichtinger, G., Forst, C. V., Piccardi, C. (1996). A nonlinear dynamical model for the dynastic cycle. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals 7, 257-271.
DynasticCycle.description: Farmers, bandits and rulers in a model of the Chinese dynastic cycle: rulers tax farmers and are hired in proportion to banditry. Slow-fast cycles alternate between despotism and anarchy, and become chaotic through period doubling.

ElectrostaticMEMS.citation: Haghighi, H. S., Markazi, A. H. D. (2010). Chaos prediction and control in MEMS resonators. Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation 15, 3091-3099.
ElectrostaticMEMS.description: A clamped-clamped microbeam resonator between two electrodes, with cubic stiffening and parallel-plate electrostatic forces from a bias plus an ac voltage. The bias creates two potential wells bounded by pull-in.

ExcitableCell.citation: Teresa Chay. Chaos In A Three-variable Model Of An Excitable Cell. Physica D 1985
ExcitableCell.description: A reduced-order variant of the Hodgkin-Huxley model. The parameter gkc controls the onset of chaos.

Finance.citation: Guoliang Cai, Juanjuan Huang. International Journal of Nonlinear Science, Vol. 3 (2007)
Finance.description: Stock fluctuations under varying investment demand and interest rates

FluidTrampoline.citation: Gilet, Bush. The fluid trampoline: droplets bouncing on a soap film. JFM 2009.
FluidTrampoline.description: A droplet bouncing on a horizontal soap film.

ForcedBrusselator.citation: I. Prigogine, From Being to Becoming: Time and Complexity in the Physical Sciences, New York: W.H. Freeman and Company, 1980.

ForcedFitzHughNagumo.citation: FitzHugh, Richard (1961). Impulses and Physiological States in Theoretical Models of Nerve Membrane. Biophysical Journal. 1 (6). Forcing parameters from Rajasekar, S., Lakshmanan, M. (1988). Period-doubling bifurcations, chaos, phase-locking and devil's staircase in a Bonhoeffer-van der Pol oscillator. Physica D 32, 146-152.
ForcedFitzHughNagumo.description: A neuron model driven by a periodic current, in the period-doubling chaotic band of the forced Bonhoeffer-van der Pol oscillator.

ForcedGlycolysis.citation: Kim, P., Hyeon, C. (2024). Glycolytic oscillations under periodic drivings. Journal of the Royal Society Interface 21, 20230588. Based on Goldbeter, A., Lefever, R. (1972). Biophysical Journal 12, 1302-1315.
ForcedGlycolysis.description: The allosteric (Monod-Wyman-Changeux) phosphofructokinase model of glycolytic oscillations, activated by its substrate and product, with a periodically modulated substrate injection rate. Concentrations in mM and time in seconds.

ForcedMPR.citation: Montbrio, E., Pazo, D., Roxin, A. (2015). Macroscopic description for networks of spiking neurons. Physical Review X 5, 021028.
ForcedMPR.description: Exact mean-field (firing rate and mean voltage) equations of an infinite network of quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons with Lorentzian heterogeneity, driven by a sinusoidal current. The forcing produces collective chaos of the spiking network.

ForcedMorrisLecar.citation: Lim, W., Kim, S.-Y., Kim, Y. (2009). Strange nonchaotic responses of the quasiperiodically forced Morris-Lecar neuron. Progress of Theoretical Physics 121, 671-683. Model from Morris, C., Lecar, H. (1981). Biophysical Journal 35, 193-213.
ForcedMorrisLecar.description: Type-II Morris-Lecar neuron (membrane potential and potassium activation) driven by a sinusoidal current, reaching chaos through period doubling. Time in ms, voltage in mV, currents in microamperes per square centimetre.

ForcedRosenzweigMacArthur.citation: Rinaldi, S., Muratori, S., Kuznetsov, Y. (1993). Multiple attractors, catastrophes and chaos in seasonally perturbed predator-prey communities. Bulletin of Mathematical Biology 55, 15-35.
ForcedRosenzweigMacArthur.description: A Rosenzweig-MacArthur predator-prey model whose prey carrying capacity varies sinusoidally with the season.

ForcedToda.citation: Kurz, T., Lauterborn, W. (1988). Bifurcation structure of the Toda oscillator. Physical Review A 37, 1029-1031.
ForcedToda.description: A sinusoidally driven damped particle in a Toda (exponential) potential; a standard model for class-B laser relaxation oscillations and nonlinear diode resonators.

ForcedVanDerPol.citation: B. van der Pol (1920). A theory of the amplitude of free and forced triode vibrations. Radio Review 1.
ForcedVanDerPol.description: An electronic circuit containing a triode.

ForcedWilsonCowan.citation: Yoshikawa, M., Ono, K., Ueta, T. (2023). Bifurcations in a forced Wilson-Cowan neuron pair. Nonlinear Theory and Its Applications, IEICE 14, 366-377. Based on Wilson, H. R., Cowan, J. D. (1972). Biophysical Journal 12, 1-24.
ForcedWilsonCowan.description: Wilson-Cowan excitatory and inhibitory population activities with logistic response functions, with a periodic input to the excitatory population. Chaos arises through torus breakdown.

GaspardNicolis.citation: Gaspard, P., Nicolis, G. (1983). What can we learn from homoclinic orbits in chaotic dynamics? Journal of Statistical Physics 31, 499-518. Rate constants from Gaspard, P. (2020). Chaos 30, 113103.
GaspardNicolis.description: An open, chemostatted network of ten reversible elementary reactions among three intermediate species, with cubic autocatalysis. A sigmoidal slow manifold with reinjection produces Shilnikov-type chaos.

GearRattle.citation: Kahraman, A., Singh, R. (1990). Non-linear dynamics of a spur gear pair. Journal of Sound and Vibration 142, 49-75.
GearRattle.description: A spur gear pair with backlash under a mean load and a periodic transmission-error excitation. The dead-zone mesh stiffness produces gear rattle; displacement is normalized by half the backlash.

GeneRegulatoryMotif.citation: Zhang, Z., Ye, W., Qian, Y., Zheng, Z., Huang, X., Hu, G. (2012). Chaotic motifs in gene regulatory networks. PLoS ONE 7, e39355.
GeneRegulatoryMotif.description: A three-gene transcriptional network built from Hill-function activation and repression: a negative feedback loop between genes 1 and 2, self-activation of gene 3, and cross-repression between genes 1, 2 and 3. A minimal chaotic gene regulatory motif; chaos requires the cross-repressions.

GenesioTesi.citation: Genesio, Tesi (1992). Harmonic balance methods for the analysis of chaotic dynamics in nonlinear systems. Automatica 28.3 (1992): 531-548.
GenesioTesi.description: A nonlinear control system with feedback.

GilpinSpiral.citation: Gilpin, M. E. (1979). Spiral chaos in a predator-prey model. The American Naturalist 113, 306-308.
GilpinSpiral.description: Two competing prey and one predator with Lotka-Volterra interactions, one of the first ecological models shown to be chaotic. All three populations are stored as logarithms because the predator falls to about 1e-16 in linear coordinates.

Gissinger.citation: Gissinger, C. (2012). A new deterministic model for chaotic reversals. European Physical Journal B 85, 137.
Gissinger.description: A three-mode model of geomagnetic reversals coupling a dipole, a quadrupole, and a symmetry-breaking velocity mode. Reversals arise through crisis-induced intermittency.

GlukhovskyDolzhansky.citation: Glukhovsky, A. B., Dolzhansky, F. V. (1980). Three component models of convection in a rotating fluid. Izvestiya, Atmospheric and Oceanic Physics 16, 311-318. Rescaled form from Leonov, G. A., Kuznetsov, N. V., Mokaev, T. N. (2015). European Physical Journal Special Topics 224, 1421-1458.
GlukhovskyDolzhansky.description: Convection of a fluid in a rotating ellipsoidal cavity, a three-mode model of ocean currents. A Lorenz-like system (Lorenz is the a = 0 case) that supports hidden attractors.

GlycolyticOscillation.citation: Decroly, O.; Goldbeter, An amplified sensitivity arising from covalent modification in biological systems. A. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 1982, 79,6917–6921.
GlycolyticOscillation.description: A model of feedback in glycolytic reactions. Based on the Monod–Wyman–Changeux model.

GuckenheimerHolmes.citation: Guckenheimer, John, and Philip Holmes (1983).  Nonlinear oscillations, dynamical systems, and bifurcations of vector fields. Vol. 42. Springer Science & Business Media.

Hadley.citation: G. Hadley (1735). On the cause of the general trade winds. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society, vol. 34, pp. 58--62.

HaimNickel.citation: Haim, D., Lev, O., Pismen, L. M., Sheintuch, M. (1992). Modeling periodic and chaotic dynamics in anodic nickel dissolution. Journal of Physical Chemistry 96, 2676-2681. Potentiostatic form and parameters from Rodrigues, R. A. et al. (2020). Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics 22, 21823-21834.
HaimNickel.description: Anodic dissolution of nickel in sulfuric acid under potentiostatic control with an external resistance: electrode potential and the surface coverages of two oxide species. The applied potential v lies in the chaotic band of Rodrigues et al. (2020). The coverages can leave the unit interval slightly, as noted by Rodrigues et al.

Halvorsen.citation: Sprott, Julien C (2010). Elegant chaos: algebraically simple chaotic flows. World Scientific, 2010.
Halvorsen.description: An algebraically-simple chaotic system with quadratic nonlinearity

HenonHeiles.citation: Henon, M.; Heiles, C. (1964). The applicability of the third integral of motion: Some numerical experiments. The Astronomical Journal. 69: 73.
HenonHeiles.description: A star's motion around the galactic center.

HideSkeldonAcheson.citation: Hide, R., Skeldon, A. C., Acheson, D. J. (1996). A study of two novel self-exciting single-disc homopolar dynamos: theory. Proceedings of the Royal Society A 452, 1369-1395.
HideSkeldonAcheson.description: A self-exciting single-disc homopolar dynamo with a series motor; a toy model of the geodynamo and of magnetic field reversals.

HindmarshRose.description: A neuron model exhibiting spiking and bursting.

Hopfield.description: A neural network with frustrated connectivity

HyperBao.citation: Bao, Liu  (2008). A hyperchaotic attractor coined from the chaotic Lu system. Chin. Physics Letters, Vol. 25, pp 2396-2399.

HyperCai.citation: Guoliang, Huang (2007). A New Finance Chaotic Attractor. International Journal of Nonlinear Science.
HyperCai.description: A hyperchaotic variant of the Finance system.

HyperJha.citation: Jürgen Meier (2003). Presentation of Attractors with Cinema.

HyperLorenz.citation: Jurgen Meier (2003). Presentation of Attractors with Cinema.
HyperLorenz.description: A hyperchaotic variant of the Lorenz attractor.

HyperLu.citation: Chen, A., Lu, J., Lu, J., & Yu, S. (2006). Generating hyperchaotic Lu attractor via state feedback control. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 364, 103-110.
HyperLu.description: A hyperchaotic variant of the Lu attractor.

HyperPang.citation: Pang, S., & Liu, Y. (2011). A new hyperchaotic system from the Lu system and its control. Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics, 235(8), 2775-2789.

HyperQi.citation: G. Qi, M. A. van Wyk, B. J. van Wyk, and G. Chen, (2008). On a new hyperchaotic system. Physics Letters A.
HyperQi.description: A hyperchaotic variant of the Qi system.

HyperRossler.citation: Rossler, O. E. (1979). An equation for hyperchaos.
HyperRossler.description: A hyperchaotic variant of the Rossler system.

HyperWang.citation: Wang, Z., Sun, Y., van Wyk, B. J., Qi, G. & van Wyk, M. A (2009). A 3-D four-wing attractor and its analysis. Brazilian J. Phys. 39.
HyperWang.description: A hyperchaotic variant of the Wang system.

HyperYan.citation: Jürgen Meier (2003). Presentation of Attractors with Cinema.

HyperYangChen.citation: Jürgen Meier (2003). Presentation of Attractors with Cinema.

Hyperion.citation: Wisdom, J., Peale, S. J., Mignard, F. (1984). The chaotic rotation of Hyperion. Icarus 58, 137-152.
Hyperion.description: Planar spin of an aspherical satellite under the gravity-gradient torque of an eccentric Keplerian orbit, which predicted the chaotic tumbling of Saturn's moon Hyperion. The orbit is advanced through its true anomaly, so the system is autonomous. Conservative, with a mixed phase space; the spin angle and anomaly are mapped through sines and cosines.

IceAgeVdPDuffing.citation: Ashwin, P., Camp, C. D., von der Heydt, A. S. (2018). Chaotic and non-chaotic response to quasiperiodic forcing: limits to predictability of ice ages paced by Milankovitch forcing. Dynamics and Statistics of the Climate System 3, dzy002. Model family from Crucifix, M. (2012). Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A 370, 1140-1165.
IceAgeVdPDuffing.description: Van der Pol-Duffing relaxation oscillator for glacial cycles, with ice volume as the slow variable and a fast hysteretic climate feedback, paced by periodic obliquity forcing (41 kyr). The unforced oscillator has a 100 kyr period. Time in kyr.

IkeuchiTomita.citation: Ikeuchi, S., Tomita, H. (1983). Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan 35, 77. See also Hirashita, H. et al. (2001). The Astrophysical Journal 552, 591.
IkeuchiTomita.description: Mass exchange among the cold, warm and hot phases of the interstellar medium, with a periodically modulated rate of supernova-driven heating. The hot-phase fraction is stored as a logarithm because it falls to about 1e-11.

InertialFitzHughNagumo.citation: Marino, F., Marin, F., Balle, S., Piro, O. (2007). Chaotically spiking canards in an excitable system with 2D inertial fast manifolds. Physical Review Letters 98, 074104.
InertialFitzHughNagumo.description: A van der Pol-FitzHugh-Nagumo excitable system in which the fast variable has inertia, giving a two-dimensional fast manifold. Canard trajectories produce chaotic spiking near the excitability threshold.

InjectedLaser.citation: Krauskopf, B., Wieczorek, S., Lenstra, D. (2000). Different types of chaos in an optically injected semiconductor laser. Applied Physics Letters 77, 1611-1613. See also Wieczorek, S. et al. (2005). Physics Reports 416, 1-128.
InjectedLaser.description: A single-mode semiconductor laser driven by a detuned master laser: the real and imaginary parts of the slave field and the carrier inversion, with amplitude-phase coupling (linewidth enhancement factor) and gain saturation.

InteriorSquirmer.citation: Blake, J. R. Self propulsion due to oscillations on the surface of a cylinder at low Reynolds number. AMS Bulletin 1971.
InteriorSquirmer.description: Boundary-driven flow of a viscous fluid within a cylinder. Any slip boundary condition can be used, as long as it is parametrized by its Fourier coefficients.

IntraguildPredation.citation: Niu, Kang, Tao, Wang (2026). A homoclinic route to chaos in omnivore communities. Communications in Theoretical Physics 78, 065601.
IntraguildPredation.description: A minimal omnivory food web: a resource, an intermediate consumer, and an omnivore that eats both, with saturating functional responses. Chaos arises from a Shilnikov homoclinic orbit. The resource growth rate r lies in the chaotic range found for the paper's Fig. 3 parameters.

IsothermalChemical.citation: Petrov, Scott, Showalter. Mixed-mode oscillations in chemical systems. J Chem Phys 1992
IsothermalChemical.description: An isothermal chemical system with mixed-mode oscillations

IteratedPrisonersDilemma.citation: You, T., Kwon, M., Jo, H.-H., Jung, W.-S., Baek, S. K. (2017). Chaos and unpredictability in evolution of cooperation in continuous time. Physical Review E 96, 062310.
IteratedPrisonersDilemma.description: Replicator-mutator dynamics of four memory-one strategies (always cooperate, always defect, tit-for-tat and win-stay-lose-shift) in the repeated prisoner's dilemma with execution errors. The state is the fractions of the last three strategies. The payoff entries a_ij are long-run payoffs for benefit 1, cost 0.453 and error rate 0.01, the point where the paper reports fully developed chaos.

ItikBanksTumor.citation: Itik, Banks. Int J Bifurcat Chaos 2010
ItikBanksTumor.description: A model of cancer cell populations.

JafariSprott.citation: Jafari, S., Sprott, J. C. (2013). Simple chaotic flows with a line equilibrium. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals 57, 79-84.
JafariSprott.description: Case LE1 of the simple chaotic flows with a line of equilibria along the z axis; a hidden attractor.

JerkCircuit.citation: Sprott (2011). A new chaotic jerk circuit. IEEE Circ. Sys. 2011.
JerkCircuit.description: An electronic circuit with nonlinearity provided by a diode.

JosephsonRCL.citation: Dana, S. K., Sengupta, D. C., Edoh, K. D. (2001). Chaotic dynamics in Josephson junction. IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I 48, 990-996. Model from Whan, C. B., Lobb, C. J. (1996). Physical Review E 53, 405-413.
JosephsonRCL.description: A dc-biased Josephson tunnel junction shunted by a series resistor and inductor: junction phase, voltage and shunt current. The quasiparticle conductance steps from its subgap to its normal value at the gap voltage; the step is smoothed with a tanh of width w = 0.05 so that adaptive integrators do not stall on the switching surface. The phase is mapped through a sine.

KarneyIonHeating.citation: Karney, C. F. F. (1978). Stochastic ion heating by a lower hybrid wave. The Physics of Fluids 21, 1584-1599.
KarneyIonHeating.description: A gyrating ion in a uniform magnetic field driven by an obliquely propagating electrostatic lower-hybrid wave, the standard model of stochastic ion heating in fusion plasmas. Conservative; orbits started below the stochastic layer are regular.

KawczynskiStrizhak.citation: P. E. Strizhak and A. L. Kawczynski, J. Phys. Chem. 99, 10830 (1995). Equations as in Goryachev, Strizhak and Kapral (1997), Slow manifold structure and the emergence of mixed-mode oscillations, J. Chem. Phys. 107, 2881.
KawczynskiStrizhak.description: A three-variable extension of the Boissonade-De Kepper model, describing mixed-mode oscillations in the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction. Chaos occurs in narrow windows between mixed-mode states and is weak.

KeynesianGrowthCycle.citation: Sportelli, M. C. (2000). Dynamic complexity in a Keynesian growth-cycle model involving Harrod's instability. Journal of Economics 71, 167-198.
KeynesianGrowthCycle.description: A Keynesian growth-cycle model with Harrod's instability principle: actual and expected growth rates and the savings rate, with productivity growth a one-hump function of the savings rate. Shilnikov-type chaos around the zero-growth equilibrium.

KlebanoffHastings.citation: Klebanoff, A., Hastings, A. (1994). Chaos in one-predator, two-prey models: general results from bifurcation theory. Mathematical Biosciences 122, 221-233.
KlebanoffHastings.description: One predator feeding on two competing prey with saturating (Holling type II) functional responses. The handling-time parameter b1 lies in the chaotic range of the paper's bifurcation diagram.

KrischerElectrochemical.citation: Nascimento, M. A., Gallas, J. A. C., Varela, H. (2011). Self-organized distribution of periodicity and chaos in an electrochemical oscillator. Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics 13, 441-446. Model from Krischer, K. (1999). Modern Aspects of Electrochemistry 32, 1-142.
KrischerElectrochemical.description: Generic electrochemical oscillator with a partially hidden negative differential resistance: double-layer potential, concentration of the reacting species at the electrode and coverage of a poisoning species. Representative of fuel-cell anode reactions such as formic acid oxidation.

Langford.citation: Langford, W. F. (1984). Numerical studies of torus bifurcations. In Numerical Methods for Bifurcation Problems (Dortmund, 1983), International Series of Numerical Mathematics 70, 285-295. Birkhauser, Basel. See also Fleurantin, E., and Mireles James, J. D. (2019). Resonant tori, transport barriers, and chaos in a vector field with a Neimark-Sacker bifurcation. arXiv:1905.08828.
Langford.description: Normal form of an interacting cusp (hysteresis) and Hopf bifurcation with an axial symmetry-breaking term, in which an invariant torus breaks up into a strange attractor.

LarterBreakspear.citation: Breakspear, M., Terry, J. R., Friston, K. J. (2003). Modulation of excitatory synaptic coupling facilitates synchronization and complex dynamics in a biophysical model of neuronal dynamics. Network: Computation in Neural Systems 14, 703-732. Based on Larter, R., Speelman, B., Worth, R. M. (1999). Chaos 9, 795-804.
LarterBreakspear.description: Conductance-based neural mass model of a cortical column, as used in The Virtual Brain: mean pyramidal-cell membrane potential, fraction of open potassium channels and inhibitory interneuron activity, with NMDA and AMPA excitatory feedback. A single uncoupled node is chaotic at the parameter set of Alstott et al. (2009) PLoS Computational Biology 5, e1000408 (gCa = 1.0, aee = 0.36, dZ = 0.65).

Laser.citation: Abooee, Yaghini-Bonabi, Jahed-Motlagh (2013). Analysis and circuitry realization of a novel three-dimensional chaotic system. Comm Nonline Sci 2013

LidDrivenCavityFlow.citation: Grover et al. Chaos (2012). Topological chaos, braiding and bifurcation of almost-cyclic sets.
LidDrivenCavityFlow.description: A two-dimensional flow alternately driven by translation of the left and right walls.

LinzSprott.citation: Linz, S. J., Sprott, J. C. (1999). Elementary chaotic flow. Physics Letters A 259, 240-245.
LinzSprott.description: The most elementary piecewise-linear chaotic jerk flow, with an absolute-value nonlinearity.

Liu.citation: Liu, C., Liu, T., Liu, L., Liu, K. (2004). A new chaotic attractor. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals 22, 1031-1038.
Liu.description: A Lorenz-like butterfly attractor with a quadratic (x^2) nonlinearity in the third equation; a standard benchmark in the synchronization and fractional-order literature.

LiuChen.citation: Liu, Chen. Int J Bifurcat Chaos. 2004: 1395-1403.

Lorenz.citation: Lorenz, Edward N (1963). Deterministic nonperiodic flow. Journal of the atmospheric sciences 20.2 (1963): 130-141.
Lorenz.description: A minimal weather model based on atmospheric convection.

Lorenz84.citation: E. Lorenz (1984). Irregularity: a fundamental property of the atmosphere. Tellus A, vol. 36, no. 2, pp. 98--110, 1984.
Lorenz84.description: Atmospheric circulation analogous to Hadley convection.

Lorenz96.citation: Lorenz, Edward (1996). Predictability: A problem partly solved. Seminar on Predictability, Vol. I, ECMWF.
Lorenz96.description: A climate model containing fluid-like advective nonlinearities, and multiscale coupling of fast and slow variables.

LorenzBounded.description: The Lorenz attractor in the presence of a confining potential.

LorenzCoupled.citation: Lorenz, Edward N. Deterministic nonperiodic flow. Journal of the atmospheric sciences 20.2 (1963): 130-141.

LuChen.citation: Lu, Chen. Int J Bifurcat Chaos. 2002: 659-661.
LuChen.description: A system that switches shapes between the Lorenz and Chen attractors as the parameter c is varied from 12.7 to 28.5. Also called the Chen Celikovsky attractor

LuChenCheng.citation: Lu, Chen, Cheng. Int J Bifurcat Chaos. 2004: 1507--1537.
LuChenCheng.description: A four scroll attractor that reduces to Lorenz-like dynamics under bifurcations.

MacArthur.citation: MacArthur, R. 1969. Species packing, and what competition minimizes. PNAS 64:1369. Parameter values taken from a model of phytoplankton in Huisman & Weissing. Nature 1999.
MacArthur.description: Population abundances in a plankton community, based on MacArthur's consumer resource model. Growth rates are determined using Liebig's law of the maximum

Malasoma.citation: Malasoma, J.-M. (2000). What is the simplest dissipative chaotic jerk equation which is parity invariant? Physics Letters A 264, 383-389.
Malasoma.description: The simplest dissipative chaotic jerk equation invariant under inversion, with a single cubic term. Its basin of attraction is small.

MankinHudson.citation: Mankin, J. C., Hudson, J. L. (1984). Oscillatory and chaotic behaviour of a forced exothermic chemical reaction. Chemical Engineering Science 39, 1807-1814.
MankinHudson.description: A first-order irreversible exothermic reaction in a cooled continuous stirred tank reactor whose coolant temperature is varied sinusoidally. The unforced reactor oscillates; increasing the forcing amplitude gives quasiperiodicity, period doubling and chaos. Dimensionless concentration and temperature (Frank-Kamenetskii limit).

MarhlCalcium.citation: Haberichter, T., Marhl, M., Heinrich, R. (2001). Birhythmicity, trirhythmicity and chaos in bursting calcium oscillations. Biophysical Chemistry 90, 17-30. Model from Marhl, M., Haberichter, T., Brumen, M., Heinrich, R. (2000). BioSystems 57, 75-86.
MarhlCalcium.description: Intracellular calcium oscillations with exchange between the cytosol, the endoplasmic reticulum and the mitochondria, and buffering by cytosolic proteins. Bursting calcium oscillations become chaotic in a window of the channel rate kch. Time in seconds, concentrations in micromolar.

McCannYodzis.citation: McCann, K., Yodzis, P. (1994). Biological conditions for chaos in a three-species food chain. Ecology 75, 561-564.
McCannYodzis.description: An allometrically scaled resource-consumer-predator food chain with Holling type II responses; a slow chaotic attractor coexisting with a resource-consumer limit cycle.

ModulatedLossLaser.citation: Arecchi, F. T., Meucci, R., Puccioni, G., Tredicce, J. (1982). Experimental evidence of subharmonic bifurcations, multistability, and turbulence in a Q-switched gas laser. Physical Review Letters 49, 1217-1220.
ModulatedLossLaser.description: A class-B laser with sinusoidally modulated cavity losses, written in log-intensity coordinates. The first variable is the logarithm of the laser intensity.

MooreSpiegel.citation: Moore, Spiegel. A Thermally Excited Nonlinear Oscillator, Ap. J., 143, 871 (1966)

MultiChua.citation: Mufcstak E. Yalcin, Johan A. K. Suykens, Joos Vandewalle. Cellular Neural Networks, Multi-Scroll Chaos And Synchronization.

MuraliLakshmananChua.citation: Murali, K., Lakshmanan, M., Chua, L. O. (1994). The simplest dissipative nonautonomous chaotic circuit. IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I 41, 462-463.
MuraliLakshmananChua.description: A sinusoidally forced series LCR circuit with a Chua diode; the simplest dissipative nonautonomous chaotic circuit.

NMRFeedbackBloch.citation: Abergel, D. (2002). Chaotic solutions of the feedback driven Bloch equations. Physics Letters A 302, 17-22.
NMRFeedbackBloch.description: Bloch equations for nuclear magnetization in a radiofrequency field, with an electronic feedback (radiation-damping) field proportional to the transverse magnetization with gain g and phase c.

NaPKKMBurster.citation: Medvedev, G. S. (2006). Transition to bursting via deterministic chaos. Physical Review Letters 97, 048102. Model from Izhikevich, E. M. (2000). International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos 10, 1171-1266.
NaPKKMBurster.description: Conductance-based neuron with a persistent sodium current, a delayed-rectifier potassium current and a slow M-type potassium current. Near the boundary between tonic spiking and square-wave bursting, a period-doubling cascade of the slow variable produces chaotic spiking. Time in ms, voltage in mV.

NewtonLiepnik.citation: Leipnik, R. B., and T. A. Newton (1981). Double strange attractors in rigid body motion with linear feedback control. Physics Letters A 86.2 (1981): 63-67.
NewtonLiepnik.description: Euler's equations for a rigid body, augmented with a linear feedback term.

NoseHoover.citation: Nose, S (1985). A unified formulation of the constant temperature molecular-dynamics methods. Journal of Chemical Physics (1984). Hoover, William G. Canonical dynamics: Equilibrium phase-space distributions. Phys. Rev. A. Hoover, William G., Anthony JC Ladd, and Bill Moran (1982). High-strain-rate plastic flow studied via nonequilibrium molecular dynamics. Physical Review Letters.
NoseHoover.description: Fixed temperature molecular dynamics for a strained flow under a reduced order model.

NuclearQuadrupole.citation: Baran V. and Raduta A. A. (1998), International Journal of Modern Physics E
NuclearQuadrupole.description: A quadrupole boson Hamiltonian that produces chaos via a resonance overlap mechanism

OneZonePulsator.citation: Saitou, M., Takeuti, M., Tanaka, Y. (1989). Chaotic behavior in nonlinear radial oscillations of one-zone stellar models. Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan 41, 297-309. See also Munteanu, A., Garcia-Berro, E., Jose, J. (2003). Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society 341, 855-862.
OneZonePulsator.description: A one-zone model of a pulsating stellar envelope with radiative luminosity and a saturating kappa-mechanism whose opacity exponents depend on the state. Radial pulsations undergo period doubling to chaos as the opacity parameter a decreases, as in RV Tauri and semi-regular variables.

OscillatingFlow.citation: T. H. Solomon and J. P. Gollub, Phys. Rev. A 38, 6280 (1988).
OscillatingFlow.description: A model fluid flow that produces KAM tori. Original parameters have been rescaled by k

PanXuZhou.citation: Zhou, Wuneng, et al. On dynamics analysis of a new chaotic attractor. Physics Letters A 372.36 (2008): 5773-5777..
PanXuZhou.description: A named attractor related to the DequanLi attractor

ParallelAutocatalator.citation: Lynch, D. T. (1992). Chaotic behavior of reaction systems: parallel cubic autocatalators. Chemical Engineering Science 47, 347-355.
ParallelAutocatalator.description: An isothermal continuous stirred tank reactor with two parallel cubic autocatalytic reactions (A + 2B to 3B and D + 2B to 3B) and decay of the autocatalyst B.

ParallelReactionCSTR.citation: Lynch, D. T., Rogers, T. D., Wanke, S. E. (1982). Chaos in a continuous stirred tank reactor. Mathematical Modelling 3, 103-116.
ParallelReactionCSTR.description: A nonadiabatic continuous stirred tank reactor with two independent first-order exothermic reactions (A to C and B to D) coupled only through the reactor temperature, with Arrhenius kinetics. The attractor is a Mobius-band type.

ParametricPendulum.citation: Leven, R. W., Koch, B. P. (1981). Chaotic behaviour of a parametrically excited damped pendulum. Physics Letters A 86, 71-74. See also Bishop, S. R., Clifford, M. J. (1996). Zones of chaotic behaviour in the parametrically excited pendulum. Journal of Sound and Vibration 189, 142-147.
ParametricPendulum.description: A damped pendulum whose pivot oscillates vertically (parametric excitation), exhibiting tumbling chaos. The angle is unbounded and mapped through a sine.

PehlivanWei.citation: Pehlivan, Ihsan, and Wei Zhouchao (2012). Analysis, nonlinear control, and chaos generator circuit of another strange chaotic system.
PehlivanWei.description: A system with quadratic nonlinearity, which undergoes Hopf bifurcations of codimension 1 and 2.

PendularCavity.citation: Marino, F., Marin, F., Balle, S., Piro, O. (2007). Chaotically spiking canards in an excitable system with 2D inertial fast manifolds. Physical Review Letters 98, 074104. Model from Marino, F., De Rosa, M., Marin, F. (2006). Physical Review E 73, 026217.
PendularCavity.description: A Fabry-Perot cavity with a pendular end mirror, in which radiation pressure competes with photothermal expansion of the mirror: mirror displacement, velocity and thermal displacement. The detuning d0 = -1.66 is in the chaotically spiking regime shown in the paper's Fig. 4.

PikovskyRabinovich.citation: Pikovsky, A. S., Rabinovich, M. I. (1978). A simple autogenerator with stochastic behaviour. Soviet Physics Doklady 23, 183-185. See also Pikovsky, A. S., Rabinovich, M. I. (1981). Stochastic oscillations in dissipative systems. Physica D 2, 8-24.
PikovskyRabinovich.description: An electronic autogenerator with a tunnel diode whose cubic current-voltage characteristic acts on a fast variable, producing relaxation-type chaos.

QIFAdaptation.citation: Pietras, B., Clusella, P., Montbrio, E. (2025). Low-dimensional model for adaptive networks of spiking neurons. Physical Review E 111, 014422.
QIFAdaptation.description: Exact mean-field equations for a network of quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons with spike-frequency adaptation: population firing rate, mean voltage and mean adaptation current. Collective chaos arises autonomously through a period-doubling cascade; eta lies inside the chaotic interval reported in the paper.

Qi.citation: G. Qi, M. A. van Wyk, B. J. van Wyk, and G. Chen, (2008). On a new hyperchaotic system. Physics Letters A.
Qi.description: A hyperchaotic system with a wide power spectrum.

QiChen.citation: Qi et al. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals 2008.
QiChen.description: A double-wing chaotic attractor that arises from two bistable attractors. The system has quadratic nonlinearity.

Rabinovich.citation: Pikovskii, A. S., Rabinovich, M. I., Trakhtengerts, V. Yu. (1978). Onset of stochasticity in decay confinement of parametric instability. Soviet Physics JETP 47, 715-719.
Rabinovich.description: Three resonantly coupled waves in a plasma, two of which are parametrically excited. A Lorenz-like system that supports coexisting self-excited and hidden attractors.

RabinovichFabrikant.citation: Rabinovich, Mikhail I.; Fabrikant, A. L. (1979). Stochastic Self-Modulation of Waves in Nonequilibrium Media. Sov. Phys. JETP.
RabinovichFabrikant.description: A reduced-order model of propagating waves in monequilibrium media.

RayleighBenard.citation: Yanagita, Kaneko (1995). Rayleigh-Bénard convection patterns, chaos, spatiotemporal chaos and turbulence. Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena 82.3 (1995): 288-313.
RayleighBenard.description: A reduced-order model of a convective cell.

RayleighDuffing.citation: Sprott, J. C. (2003). Chaos and Time-Series Analysis. Oxford University Press, Appendix A.
RayleighDuffing.description: A periodically forced Duffing oscillator with Rayleigh (velocity-cubed) self-excitation instead of van der Pol damping.

RedQueen.citation: Dercole, F., Ferriere, R., Rinaldi, S. (2010). Chaotic Red Queen coevolution in three-species food chains. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 277, 2321-2330.
RedQueen.description: Coevolution of the traits of a resource, consumer and predator under the canonical equation of adaptive dynamics, with population densities slaved to their ecological equilibrium. Chaos arises in evolutionary trait space (a chaotic Red Queen) through a period-doubling cascade in the resource's evolutionary rate.

RfSquid.citation: Hizanidis, J., Lazarides, N., Tsironis, G. P. (2018). Flux bias-controlled chaos and extreme multistability in SQUID oscillators. Chaos 28, 063117.
RfSquid.description: A radiofrequency superconducting quantum interference device (a superconducting loop with one Josephson junction) driven by ac and dc magnetic flux. The linear inductive term creates a multiwell potential, and the dc flux breaks its symmetry.

RikitakeDynamo.citation: Rikitake, T., Oscillations of a system of disk dynamos, Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society, 1958.
RikitakeDynamo.description: Electric current and magnetic field of two coupled disk dynamos.

Rossler.citation: Rossler, O. E. (1976), An Equation for Continuous Chaos, Physics Letters, 57A (5): 3972013398,
Rossler.description: Spiral-type chaos in a simple oscillator model.

RosslerPrototype4.citation: Rossler, O. E. (1979). Continuous chaos - four prototype equations. Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences 316, 376-392.
RosslerPrototype4.description: Rossler's fourth prototype equation, with a single quadratic term; produces toroidal chaos.

Rucklidge.citation: Rucklidge, A.M. (1992). Chaos in models of double convection. Journal of Fluid Mechanics.
Rucklidge.description: Two-dimensional convection in a horizontal layer of Boussinesq fluid with lateral constraints.

Sakarya.citation: Li, Chunbiao, et al (2015). A novel four-wing strange attractor born in bistability. IEICE Electronics Express 12.4.
Sakarya.description: An attractor that arises due to merging of two disjoint bistable attractors.

SaltonSea.citation: Upadhyay, Bairagi, Kundu, Chattopadhyay (2007).Chaos in eco-epidemiological problem of the Salton Sea and its possible control. Applied mathematics and computation.
SaltonSea.description: An eco-epidemiological model of bird and fish abundances in the Salton sea of southern California.

SanUmSrisuchinwong.description: A two-scroll attractor arising from dynamical equations with piecewise nonlinearities. Equivalent to the Wimol-Banlue system

SaturableAbsorberLaser.citation: Lefranc, M., Hennequin, D., Dangoisse, D. (1991). Homoclinic chaos in a laser containing a saturable absorber. Journal of the Optical Society of America B 8, 239-249.
SaturableAbsorberLaser.description: A CO2 laser with an intracavity saturable absorber, in the limit where the absorber follows the intensity adiabatically: intensity, amplifier population inversion and the population of a third coupled level. Produces Shilnikov-type homoclinic pulsing (passive Q-switching).

SchefferDaphnia.citation: Scheffer, M., Rinaldi, S., Kuznetsov, Y. A., van Nes, E. H. (1997). Seasonal dynamics of Daphnia and algae explained as a periodically forced predator-prey system. Oikos 80, 519-532.
SchefferDaphnia.description: Algae and Daphnia in a lake with seasonally varying temperature and light, a sigmoidal fish predation term on Daphnia and an algal refuge. Time in days. The forcing strength and fish predation lie near the boundary of the region where the paper reports erratic long cycles.

SeasonalSIR.citation: Kuznetsov, Y. A., Piccardi, C. (1994). Bifurcation analysis of periodic SEIR and SIR epidemic models. Journal of Mathematical Biology 32, 109-121. Parameters from Keeling, M. J., Rohani, P. (2008). Modeling Infectious Diseases in Humans and Animals. Princeton University Press.
SeasonalSIR.description: A susceptible-infected-recovered epidemic with births and deaths and a sinusoidally varying contact rate (school terms), with measles-like parameters: basic reproduction number 22, a 13-day infectious period and a 70-year lifespan. Time in years. The infected fraction is stored as a logarithm because it falls to about 1e-26 between epidemics.

ShawVanDerPol.citation: Shaw, R. (1981). Strange attractors, chaotic behavior, and information flow. Zeitschrift fur Naturforschung A 36, 80-112.
ShawVanDerPol.description: Shaw's variant of the forced Van der Pol oscillator, in which the forcing enters the velocity equation; produces a toroidal (bagel-shaped) attractor.

ShenLarter.citation: Perc, M., Marhl, M. (2003). Sensitivity and flexibility of regular and chaotic calcium oscillations. Biophysical Chemistry 104, 509-522. Model from Shen, P., Larter, R. (1995). Cell Calcium 17, 225-232.
ShenLarter.description: Calcium oscillations driven by both calcium-induced calcium release and IP3-dependent release from the endoplasmic reticulum, with cytosolic calcium, stored calcium and IP3 as variables. The stimulation level r lies inside one of the chaotic windows reported in the paper. Time in seconds.

ShimizuMorioka.description: A system that bifurcates from a symmetric limit cycle to an asymmetric one, similar to the Lorenz attractor.

SpinValveOscillator.citation: Yang, Z., Zhang, S., Li, Y. C. (2007). Chaotic dynamics of spin-valve oscillators. Physical Review Letters 99, 134101.
SpinValveOscillator.description: Macrospin Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics of the free layer of a spin valve under a spin-transfer torque from a dc plus ac current, in spherical angles. Fields are scaled by the saturation magnetization and time by the corresponding precession rate; the forcing frequency is the paper's 15 GHz read as an angular frequency.

SprottA.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottA.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottB.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottB.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottC.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottC.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottD.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottD.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottE.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottE.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottF.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottF.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottG.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottG.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottH.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottH.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottI.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottI.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottJ.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottJ.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottJerk.citation: Sprott, J. C. Simplest dissipative chaotic flow. Physics Letters A (1997).
SprottJerk.description: An algebraidally simple flow depending on a third time derivative. Numerical integration of this attractor is extremely sensitive to the initial conditions

SprottK.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottK.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottL.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottL.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottM.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottM.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottMore.citation: Sprott, J. C. (2020). Do We Need More Chaos Examples? Chaos Theory and Applications 2(2),1-3, 2020.
SprottMore.description: A multifractal system with a nearly 3D attractor

SprottN.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottN.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottO.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottO.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottP.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottP.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottQ.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottQ.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottR.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottR.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottS.citation: Sprott (1994). Some simple chaotic flows. Physical Review E (1994).
SprottS.description: A member of the Sprott family of algebraically-simple chaotic sytems.

SprottTorus.description: A multiattractor system that goes to a torus or a complex attractor depending on the initial conditions.

StickSlipOscillator.citation: Awrejcewicz, Jan, and M. M. Holicke (1999). Int J of Bifurcation and Chaos.
StickSlipOscillator.description: A weakly forced (quasiautonomous) oscillator with dynamics similar to stick-slip friction. The parameter gamma controls the transition to chaos.

StokesDrop.citation: Stone, H. A., Nadim, A., Strogatz, S. H. (1991). Chaotic streamlines inside drops immersed in steady Stokes flows. Journal of Fluid Mechanics 232, 629-646.
StokesDrop.description: Streamlines of the steady internal circulation of a spherical drop held in a linear external Stokes flow combining strain and vorticity. The flow is volume-preserving and bounded by the unit sphere, so particle paths fill a chaotic sea with regular islands.

StretchTwistFold.citation: Bajer, K., Moffatt, H. K. (1990). On a class of steady confined Stokes flows with chaotic streamlines. Journal of Fluid Mechanics 212, 337-363. Parameters from Yue, B. Z., Aqeel, M. (2013). Chinese Science Bulletin 58, 1655-1662.
StretchTwistFold.description: A steady, volume-preserving Stokes flow in the unit sphere that performs the stretch-twist-fold action of fast magnetic dynamos. Streamlines are chaotic.

SugamaHorton.citation: Sugama, H., Horton, W. (1995). L-H confinement mode dynamics in three-dimensional state space. Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion 37, 345-362. See also Ball, R., Dewar, R. L., Sugama, H. (2002). Physical Review E 66, 066408.
SugamaHorton.description: Energy exchange at the edge of a tokamak between the pressure gradient, resistive-interchange turbulence and sheared poloidal flow, modelling the L-H confinement transition and edge-localized modes. The turbulence and flow energies are stored as logarithms because the flow energy falls to about 1e-17 during bursts.

SugunaSinha.citation: Suguna, C., Chowdhury, K. K., Sinha, S. (1999). Minimal model for complex dynamics in cellular processes. Physical Review E 60, 5943-5949.
SugunaSinha.description: A three-step metabolic pathway in which the end product represses synthesis of the first substrate cooperatively and activates the second step through an allosteric (Monod-Wyman-Changeux) enzyme. Chaotic oscillations occur in a window of the degradation rate k.

SwingingAtwood.citation: Tufillaro, Nicholas B.; Abbott, Tyler A.; Griffiths, David J. (1984). Swinging Atwood's Machine. American Journal of Physics. 52 (10): 895--903.
SwingingAtwood.description: A mechanical system consisting of two swinging weights connected by ropes and pulleys. This is only chaotic when m2 is sufficiently larger than m1, and there are nonzero initial momenta

SymmetricGyro.citation: Chen, H.-K. (2002). Chaos and chaos synchronization of a symmetric gyro with linear-plus-cubic damping. Journal of Sound and Vibration 255, 719-740. See also Van Dooren, R. (2003). Journal of Sound and Vibration 268, 632-634.
SymmetricGyro.description: A symmetric heavy gyroscope with linear-plus-cubic damping on a vertically vibrating base. The forcing amplitude f = 35 lies in the chaotic range computed by Van Dooren (2003), where the two symmetric chaotic attractors have merged. The gyroscopic term is written in a form that is regular at zero nutation angle.

Thomas.citation: Thomas, Rene (1999). Deterministic chaos seen in terms of feedback circuits: Analysis, synthesis, labyrinth chaos. Int. J. Bifurc. Chaos.
Thomas.description: A cyclically-symmetric attractor correspondng to a frictionally-damped particle traversing a 3D lattice of forces

ThomasLabyrinth.citation: Thomas, Rene. Deterministic chaos seen in terms of feedback circuits: Analysis, synthesis, labyrinth chaos. Int. J. Bifurc. Chaos. (1999).
ThomasLabyrinth.description: A system in which trajectories seemingly undergo Brownian motion on an infinite lattice, but remain bounded when the parameter a is less than one.

ThreeWaveDecay.citation: Wersinger, J.-M., Finn, J. M., Ott, E. (1980). Bifurcation and strange behavior in instability saturation by nonlinear three-wave mode coupling. Physics of Fluids 23, 1142-1154. Parameters from Viana, R. L. et al. (2012). International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos 22, 1250234.
ThreeWaveDecay.description: Saturation of a linearly unstable plasma wave by decay into two damped daughter waves with a frequency mismatch, reduced to three variables on the invariant manifold of equal daughter amplitudes. The daughter-wave energy is stored as a logarithm because it falls to about 1e-24 between bursts.

Tigan.citation: Tigan, G., Opris, D. (2008). Analysis of a 3D chaotic system. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals 36, 1315-1319.
Tigan.description: The T system, a Lorenz-like quadratic system that interpolates between Lorenz-type and Chen-type dynamics.

TimmermannJin.citation: Timmermann, A., Jin, F.-F., Abshagen, J. (2003). A nonlinear theory for El Nino bursting. Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences 60, 152-165.
TimmermannJin.description: A nonlinear recharge-oscillator model of ENSO coupling western and eastern Pacific temperatures with the western thermocline depth. A tanh closure for upwelled water produces Shilnikov-type bursts of extreme El Nino events. Time is in days. The parameter eps controls zonal advection and has narrow chaotic windows.

Torus.citation: See, for example, Strogatz (1994). Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos.
Torus.description: A minimal quasiperiodic flow on a torus. All lyapunov exponents and related quantities are zero

Tsucs2.citation: Pan, Zhou, Li (2013). Synchronization of Three-Scroll Unified Chaotic System (TSUCS) and its hyper-chaotic system using active pinning control
Tsucs2.description: A named attractor related to the DequanLi attractor

TurchinHanski.citation: Turchin, Hanski. The American Naturalist 1997. Turchin, Hanski. Ecology 2000
TurchinHanski.description: A chaotic three species food web. The species growth rate has been increased from the default parameters in the original paper, in order to ensure that the system exhibits sustained chaotic oscillations.

TwoWaveParticle.citation: Escande, D. F., Doveil, F. (1981). Renormalization method for computing the threshold of the large-scale stochastic instability in two degrees of freedom Hamiltonian systems. Journal of Statistical Physics 26, 257-284. Parameters from Doveil, F., Macor, A., Elskens, Y. (2006). Chaos 16, 033103.
TwoWaveParticle.description: A charged particle moving in two electrostatic waves with different phase velocities, the paradigm of large-scale chaos from overlapping resonances, realised experimentally in traveling-wave tubes. Hamiltonian; the position and time phase are mapped through sines.

UedaAkamatsu.citation: Ueda, Y., Akamatsu, N. (1981). Chaotically transitional phenomena in the forced negative-resistance oscillator. IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems 28, 217-224.
UedaAkamatsu.description: A forced negative-resistance (single-well Duffing-Van der Pol) oscillator, producing the broken-egg attractor.

UnifiedChaotic.citation: Lu, J., Chen, G., Cheng, D., Celikovsky, S. (2002). Bridge the gap between the Lorenz system and the Chen system. International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos 12, 2917-2926.
UnifiedChaotic.description: A one-parameter family that is chaotic for all alpha in [0, 1], with alpha = 0 giving Lorenz, alpha = 0.8 Lu, and alpha = 1 Chen. The intermediate value alpha = 0.5 is used here.

UpadhyayRai.citation: Upadhyay, R. K., Rai, V. (1997). Why chaos is rarely observed in natural populations. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals 8, 1933-1939. Holling type IV form from Upadhyay, R. K., Raw, S. N. (2011). Complex dynamics of a three species food-chain model with Holling type IV functional response. Nonlinear Analysis: Modelling and Control 16, 353-374.
UpadhyayRai.description: A three-species food chain with Holling type IV (group defence) functional responses.

VallisElNino.citation: Vallis GK. Conceptual models of El Nio and the southern oscillation. J Geophys Res 1988
VallisElNino.description: Atmospheric temperature fluctuations with annual forcing.

WangChen.citation: Wang, X., Chen, G. (2012). A chaotic system with only one stable equilibrium. Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation 17, 1264-1272.
WangChen.description: A hidden chaotic attractor coexisting with a single stable equilibrium point. Reduces to Sprott E when a = 0.

WangSun.citation: Wang, Z., Sun, Y., van Wyk, B. J., Qi, G. & van Wyk, M. A (2009). A 3-D four-wing attractor and its analysis. Brazilian J. Phys. 39.

WattGovernor.citation: Ge, Z.-M., Yang, H.-S., Chen, H.-H., Chen, H.-K. (1999). Regular and chaotic dynamics of a rotational machine with a centrifugal governor. International Journal of Engineering Science 37, 921-943.
WattGovernor.description: A steam engine regulated by a fly-ball (Watt) governor: the angle and angular velocity of the governor arms and the engine speed. The arm angle sets the fuel valve. Chaos arises through period doubling below the Hopf point.

Wei.citation: Wei, Z. (2011). Dynamical behaviors of a chaotic system with no equilibria. Physics Letters A 376, 102-108.
Wei.description: The first dissipative chaotic flow with no equilibrium points; a canonical hidden-attractor example derived from Sprott D.

WienBridge.citation: Namajunas, A., Tamasevicius, A. (1995). Modified Wien-bridge oscillator for chaos. Electronics Letters 31, 335-336.
WienBridge.description: A Wien-bridge oscillator with an additional capacitor and a piecewise-linear diode nonlinearity, in the dimensionless form of the paper with the parameters of its Fig. 2a. The attractor is unimodal and bounded by a genus-one torus.

WillamowskiRossler.citation: Willamowski, K.-D., Rossler, O. E. (1980). Irregular oscillations in a realistic abstract quadratic mass action system. Zeitschrift fur Naturforschung A 35, 317-318.
WillamowskiRossler.description: A three-species mass-action chemical reaction network with autocatalysis, the canonical example of chemical chaos. Parameter values follow Geysermans and Nicolis.

WindmiReduced.citation: Smith, Thiffeault, Horton. J Geophys Res. 2000. Horton, Weigel, Sprott. Chaos 2001.
WindmiReduced.description: Energy transfer into the ionosphere and magnetosphere by the solar wind. The parameter vsw controls the onset of chaos.

YuWang.citation: Yu, Wang (2012). A novel three dimension autonomous chaotic system with a quadratic exponential nonlinear term. Eng Techn & Applied Science Research.
YuWang.description: A temperature-compensation circuit with an operational amplifier

YuWang2.citation: Yu, Wang (2012). A novel three dimension autonomous chaotic system with a quadratic exponential nonlinear term. Eng Techn & Applied Science Research.
YuWang2.description: An alternative temperature-compensation circuit with an operational amplifier

ZhouChen.citation: Zhou, Chen (2004). A simple smooth chaotic system with a 3-layer attractor. Int J Bifurcat Chaos, 2004
